_doc: Gate lifecycle metadata -- WR-000019 slice S5.

One entry per gate script actually wired in ops/config/hooks.json (35 gates as of 2026-09-01, re-derived from hooks.json at that date -- WR-000019 slice S3 retired canonical-edit-gate.py, git-writer-gate.py and staging-attribution-gate.py on 2026-08-27, and canonical-edit-gate.py was REINSTATED on 2026-09-01 by Joe's ruling 7f48abf6 while the other two stay retired; the count is re-derivable any time by walking that file the same way ops/hook-telemetry-rollup.py's wiring() does). A gate wired ONLY through .claude/settings.json (worktree-self-plumb.py, machine-converge.py) is a different wiring surface and out of this slice's DoD wording -- it is not listed here.

delegation-gate.py IS listed, as of WR-000019 slice S4 (2026-08-27), despite being wired only through .claude/settings.json (PreToolUse and, as of this slice, Stop) rather than ops/config/hooks.json -- an intentional, named exception to the line above. This slice's own DoD asked for the gate's mode recorded here, and ops/gate-lifecycle-report.py's coverage check treats a metadata entry for a gate absent from ops/config/hooks.json's wired set as a non-fatal 'stale_metadata' WARNING rather than a failure (see that script's own docstring), so recording it costs nothing. Its catch_metric points at its own dedicated out/delegation-gate-ledger.jsonl rather than the shared out/hook-telemetry.jsonl register convention every ops/config/hooks.json-wired gate uses, for the same reason completion-evidence-gate.py and map-architecture-gate.py keep dedicated logs: it was never part of that shared wiring surface to begin with.

failure_class   one line, what this gate exists to catch. Reused verbatim from ops/config/hook-catch-classes.json's catch_class where an entry already existed there (36 of 38); the two gaps (rule-pack-preuse-reselection.py, rule-pack-drift-gate.py) are new one-liners drawn from the gate's own docstring.

catch_metric    where a real catch is visible in a log already on disk, and the rule for recognizing one there. See ops/gate-lifecycle-report.py's module docstring for the exact evaluator per true_positive.kind.

review_date     a static calendar checkpoint (90 days from admission, uniform first pass -- provisional, like the rollup's BUDGET_MS). A downgrade/retirement PROPOSAL from the weekly report can and should trigger review earlier than this date; this date is the backstop for a gate the report never flags.

mode            enforcing | announce | shadow, matching ops/hook-meter-run.py's own register vocabulary (block/reopen vs announce vs silent). Determined from the gate's OWN source (a live sys.exit(2) / return 2 / {'decision':'block'} / permissionDecision deny-or-ask path reachable in current code == enforcing; a live additionalContext-only path == announce; no live surfaced effect == shadow), cross-checked against the two gates that self-declare shadow status in their own docstrings (rule-pack-preuse-reselection.py, rule-pack-drift-gate.py). The 2026-08-23 rationing demoted map-architecture/context-handoff/stale-claim/loose-work/unread-artifact-gate.py, leaving three Stop reopeners. A0c deliberately restores context-handoff-gate.py as the fourth reopener only at a measured context threshold without a verified same-task takeover; map-architecture, stale-claim, loose-work and unread-artifact remain announcers.

THIS FILE PROPOSES NOTHING BY ITSELF. ops/gate-lifecycle-report.py reads it plus the logs above and computes proposals; nothing here changes a gate's actual wiring or mode -- that stays a human/PR act.

'conduct-stop-gate.py:chat-writing-shadow' IS a second intentional, documented exception to the one-entry-per-wired-gate-script convention (the same shape delegation-gate.py's entry above already carries), added WR-000019 slice S8. It is not a second gate SCRIPT -- it is a NEW check folded into the existing conduct-stop-gate.py (rule 5be2f462's vocab/contrast-reframe/contrast-reframe-split constructions, reusing chat-lint-gate.py's own writing_rules() rather than a second copy of the regex table), born shadow rather than consuming another Stop reopener. The 2026-08-23 rationing originally capped reopeners at three; A0c explicitly ratifies context-handoff-gate.py as the fourth, narrowly at the measured lifecycle threshold. Its mode flag is read directly by that new code path -- ops/gate-lifecycle-report.py's coverage check will list this key under stale_metadata (a name absent from ops/config/hooks.json's wired-script set), which is expected and non-fatal for exactly the reason the delegation-gate.py note above gives. Promotion to enforcing is Joe's act, same as every other gate in this file; nothing here changes conduct-stop-gate.py's OWN top-level entry (mode enforcing, unchanged) or its existing blocking classes.

catch_metric.rule_description: every row in out/conduct-gate-shadow.jsonl is a genuine 5be2f462 finding on the turn's own final assistant message -- shadow_writing_check() in hooks/conduct-stop-gate.py only writes when _writing_shadow_findings() actually matched a HARD rule from writing-lint.py's RULES table; presence in the window is the catch, the same row_exists convention chat-lint-gate.py's own entry above uses.
catch_metric.note: dedicated log, deliberately separate from out/conduct-gate.jsonl -- that log's catch_metric for conduct-stop-gate.py's own entry treats every row as a genuine BLOCKING detection, and a log-only shadow finding must never be counted there.

drift-assertion-gate.py.failure_class: drift asserted at turn end without a record

catch_metric.rule_description: a hook-guard.log line 'drift-assertion-gate BLOCK hits=N' -- the gate actually reopened the turn over an unrecorded drift assertion. Unlike drift-claim-gate.py's log() (which prefixes every line with an ISO timestamp), this gate's own log() writes `f"drift-assertion-gate {line}\n"` with NO leading timestamp (checked 2026-08-27, hooks/drift-assertion-gate.py:118-119) -- so a windowed true-positive count cannot be computed from this log at all, and is reported as a data gap rather than guessed at zero.
catch_metric.note: same execve situation as drift-claim-gate.py (see its note: this gate never reaches out/hook-telemetry.jsonl either), PLUS its own hook-guard.log lines carry no timestamp -- a real observability gap in the gate's own logging, worth a follow-up, but hooks/*.py is out of this slice's scope to edit.

catch_metric.rule_description: a hook-guard.log line 'TS drift-claim-gate CONTEXT tool=... hits=N' -- the gate injected its verification reminder because a completion/drift claim needed a fresh record behind it.
catch_metric.note: run-record-gate.py execve's this gate, replacing the process before hook-meter-run.py's own telemetry write runs, so it never appears in out/hook-telemetry.jsonl (confirmed empty for hook== 'run-record-gate.py' during this slice's research). out/hook-guard.log is a plain-text log ('TS name VERDICT(class) detail' per line, no ts field to parse structurally) -- true_positive matches the line shape directly instead of a JSON field.
